Robots automation has been around for a long time. I don't understand all the hype now. Perhaps some anti-union propaganda being spread around around with all the talk of 15 dollar minimum wages.

Robots automation has been around for a long time.

They have, yes, but the previous generation were slow and stupid. They were able to automate simple, repetitive tasks, but only those tasks they were programmed for. Enter the new generation of multi-taski, multi-purpose robots like Baxter who learn a task by watching and can actually think through the process and improve on it with no further programming.

It's the difference between mechanical muscle and mechanical mind. Think about transportation. The internal combustion engine replaced the horse, now we're replacing the driver. Think about how close the self-driving car is; they've already driven a million plus miles on the road in California and caused zero accidents. Take individual consumers out of the equation and focus on truck drivers, taxis, shuttles, buses, anyone who's employed to drive. That's two or three million jobs in the US alone. And that's just the transportation industries because they're the low hanging fruit. The most obvious and probably most immediate. But also think about warehouse workers that are already being affected by these guys, dock and port workers and miners.

What it boils down to is that the previous automation revolution saw a replacement of mindless repetitive tasks, but anything requiring decision making, judgement calls or any kind of learning still required a high level of human intervention. We're seeing that changing and things that we thought could never be automated are being automated at a pretty substantial and shocking rate. I'm not weighing in here on whether it's good or bad, but I will say that it's inevitable.

It's funny when you compare what happens in places like China and the UK (where I reside). In China it's just like, "hey workers, we have robots now, so you go away now". However in the UK, if you try firing anyone, there'll be strikes and riots over "job cuts", and in the end, the workers will probably be able to actually swindle a pay rise out of it. And don't forget lawsuits for "emotional turmoil" over just the prospect of job cuts.

Pretty large difference in worker mentality.

That's what happen when Marxists become established as the governing class. All of the sudden the general strikes become evil, after all they were just a means of bankrupting the bourgeoisie, wasn't it, how dare they use the same tactics against a "democratic" regime.

Unions can be very good in order to negotiate better conditions, a means for employees to group and talk to their employer, and negotiate contracts, like normal people do.

What's awful IMO is that Corporativist thing they have became now in most countries, where people are forced into supporting or joining labor unions and their desire become the law of the land, where government uses them to control employer-employee relations, or even in more extreme cases they can become a Government sanctioned mob. Sadly, in a lot of places the Fascist ideology won the war in that regard.

Doing this in low wage, low worker safety places is an indication that there will be lots more humans without a means of providing for themselves. I guess that the expectation is that they will now be free to write poetry and devise the next big technological advances.
